Basket (.1) and lid (.2). Both parts with circular opening reinforced with a strip of wood carved in low relief with geometric designs; raised areas pigmented black. Body of basket and lid woven in twill pattern with strips of cane. Wider strips of cane sewn below wooden panels. Rim of .1 damaged with fragments detached but present.
A wooden porridge ladle, with a round bowl and rectangular handle that tapers to a downwards curved point. The handle has section carved with zig-zags between parallel lines with black pigment.
Uta. Small toy bow with a wooden bow and twisted fibre string tied around both terminals. The string has broken at one end.

Wooden mallet or beater used for manufacturing barkcloth, comprising a sub-cylindrical head [.1], and a handle formed of a split wooden cylinder [.2]. One end of the head is flat with an incised cross hatched pattern, the other end is tapered and rounded. The head is wrapped with plant fibre twine, for fastening the head to the handle. Plant fibre is tied around the bottom and middle of the handle.
A wooden walking stick with a short rectangular handle and carved figure on the back, possibly a lizard.
Walking stick made of carved wood. The top is a tapered cylinder with grooves below which is a wider, ridged cylindrical area. The body has a circular cross-section, with a slightly flared foot.
A wooden spoon with a small shallow bowl and long handle with rectangular cross section. The end of the handle is carved in a diamond shape.
A wooden spoon with a large, slightly square bowl, handle with a rectangular cross section, and a carved 'v' shaped projection at the end.
A wooden spoon with a deep scoop and a flat rectangular handle. The handle is carved with short parallel grooves and crossing lines, and decorated with black pigment.
Snuff box. Wooden pedestal foot, carved decoration. Straight sides, cylindrical with  affixed with iron nails. The neck is narrow carved wood with an upright rim.

Bullet pouch in three pieces, one of which fits inside the other to form a large container holding a smaller oval pouch. Woven of flat strips of plant material in a twill pattern. To contain bullets (.2).

Carved bamboo snuff container with tassels. The cylindrical bamboo container is carved with intricate triangles, starts and zig zag decoration. With three rows of brass studs. Tied to one end is a long section of cloth that divides into tassels, one with a stopper for the container, the other with tied bundles.
Bamboo snuff container. Hollow cylindrical length of bamboo, carved on the outside with bands of zig zag decoration. Closed at one end.
A wooden spoon with a small shallow bowl and long handle with rectangular cross section. The end of the handle is carved in a diamond shape.

Seat or stool of a chief. Curved seat decorated with two carved lizards in high relief, coloured black with eyes of white glass beads. Two legs with openwork geometric design. Several large cracks on one side have been repaired with broad metal strips.
12 toy arrows made from lengths of dried reed. Two pointed at the ends, 10 blunt.
A wooden walking stick with a short rectangular handle and carved figure on the back, possibly a lizard.
20 iron bullets of uneven shape, contained within a woven pouch (.1).

instruments.title: Part of a string instrument, likely a simple stick zither. It has a long wooden neck, with rod-like protrusions at one end; two at the very end, one at one side, and two at the other side. Originally there would have been three at each side, but some have broken off and are missing. The other end bends to a curved tip, although the end has broken off. The neck is highly decorated with intricate geometric carvings. The strings are now missing, and it is possible that there was once a resonator, possibly of gourd, attached; however, this is also missing.

Dance rattle made from 16 small, spherical gourds arranged in four rows. Each row of four is threaded onto a cane stick, which are all attached to each other at either end using strips of fabric. The gourds contain pellets, likely made from seeds, that create the rattling sound. Some of the gourds are cracked and damaged and their seeds have fallen out and are missing.

Dance rattle, made from 37 small, spherical gourds strung onto a long piece of plant fibre rope. Each gourd has a hole through the middle and a tube, possibly of cane, has been inserted into the hole. This prevents the seeds that are inside the gourd from falling out. The gourds are threaded onto a long piece of plant fibre rope, which is presumably how the rattle would be operated. Some of the gourds are cracked and damaged, and there is an additional gourd that is detached but present.

A wooden drum, squat and cylindrical, with a stepped base that is narrower than the body. A skin is stretched over the top and down the sides, where is is held in place with wooden pegs. There is a small hole in each side, through which a plant fibre rope is threaded.

Drum, with a short, stepped cylindrical body and five legs, carved as a whole from one piece of wood. The legs curve out slightly at the bottom and have a carved, triangular cut-out section near the top; they are quite long, making up over half the height of the drum overall. There is a skin stretched over the top of the drum, which is held in place with wooden pegs. There is a circular depression in the middle of the skin, likely caused by the drum being played with a beater.

garment.title: Belt of buffalo skin, with three cartridge pouches attached (one of which is made of the skin of an elephant's ear, one is closed with a red glass bead toggle). Both the belt and two of the pouches are decorated with stamped ornament. Belt secured with a small metal buckle.
Rectangular beaded apron with a black beaded waistband and blue beaded fringe. The central pattern is panels of triangles in black, white, dark blue, yellow, light blue, pink and green glass beads.
Long beaded belt with black, light blue, dark blue, pink and white glass beads making a diamond pattern. Plaited plant fibre tassels at both ends.

Woman's beaded apron, rectangular with zigzags in blue, green, white, black, pink and orange glass beads. Blue beaded fringe along the bottom edge. These aprons are only worn in the house by married women.
Woven belt with horizontal rows of blue and white glass beads, forming a continuous loop.

Small beaded apron. Rectangular with a hanging black and yellow beaded fringe along the bottom edge. Separate string of blue glass beads along the top edge, attached at both corners. The pattern is pink, black and blue triangles bordered with yellow, black and white beads.
Beaded belt, made from light blue, dark blue, red and white beads in horizontal stripes. Narrow belt that forms a continuos loop.

jewelry.title: Headband of white, brown, green, yellow, pink and blue glass beads arranged into chevron patterns.
Necklace made up of a cord of beads, organised in blocks of colour; white, blue and light blue glass beads.
Necklace of red, white, blue, and black glass beads. The white and red beads are organised in flower patterns, with blocks of blue or black beads between; also six larger beads in the same colours.
Necklace of plaited strings of blue and white glass beads with four larger glass beads in red and blue.
Necklace of brown and white glass beads, mostly spherical in shape and strung onto a fibre cord.
Headband of pink, light and dark blue, white, and red glass beads; single strand of beads interspersed with diamond sections.
Headband of yellow, green, orange, red, white and blue glass beads. The beads are arrange in an open-work pattern with alternating white and blue beads between the loops.
Headband of pink, green, blue, red and white beads. The red and white beads are organised in a floral designs interspersed with alternating blocks of coloured beads.
Necklace of red, white, and blue glass beads. The white and red beads are organised in flower patterns, with blocks of blue beads between.

arms.title: Knife [.1] and sheath [.2]. The blade has a straight back and curved cutting edge with a fuller near the back. The blade is set into a dark, wooden handle and secured with rivets. The sheath is made of wood, bound with hide stitched along one edge; terminal of the sheath is uncovered.

Spear with wooden shaft and metal, probably iron, spearhead. Elongated, leaf-shaped blade with midrib and point bent slightly upwards. Closed metal socket with dot work and wavy bands in raised relief around circumference. Shaft has circular cross-section and terminates in wedge-shaped ferrule, probably also of iron, with similar closed metal socket.

Yao. Wooden spear shaft made of multiple pieces with iron blade. Below the blade, there is a hexagonal cylinder connecting the blade to the shaft. The shaft has a circular cross-section and is carved with lines and squares at both ends. The termination is made from one carved cylinder followed by a smaller iron cylinder and a short implement.

Yao. Wooden spear shaft made of multiple pieces with iron concave tip blade. Below the blade, there is a hexagonal cylinder connecting the blade to the shaft. The shaft has a circular cross-section and is carved with geometrical patterns including 'x' lines and squares at both ends. The termination is made from one  long carved iron cylinder.

masks-ritual.title: Knobkerry with a spherical head and handle with a circular cross-section. The handle has a carved double twine design.

textile.title: Large, sub-rectangular dark reddish-brown piece of barkcloth, with black geometric patterning on one side. Made of five lengths of barkcloth sewn together with patches of similar barkcloth stitched in. The central design has a background of very small crescents and a motif of larger, thicker, chevrons organised into seven horizontal rows. This is wholly framed by concentric rectangles, one of which is filled with diagonal lines.

Large, rectangular dark reddish-brown piece of barkcloth with black geometric patterning on one side. The major designs in the centre consist of a background of small dots in concentric circles, fairly regularly applied, and a motif of four vertical columns of six pointed stars with circles and spots at their centre. This is wholly framed by straight lines forming concentric rectangles, within which dots and diagonal lines are drawn.

Large dark brown piece of barkcloth, made of three lengths of cloth stitched together. Decorated with a central panel of chevrons enclosed in a grid bordered with dots and diagonal lines. Several small square patches sewn in.

Piece of barkcloth, vertically striped reddish-brown, very dark brown, and a grey-brown in three sections, separated by two solid sections of very dark brown. Two straight edges, two natural. Long fibres not fully beaten in.

Sub-rectangular, dark reddish-brown piece of barkcloth with black patterning on one side. The pattern in the centre consist of vertical zigzag lines, framed by straight lines that form concentric rectangles.
Large, sub-rectangular, light brown piece of barkcloth. The barkcloth is fairly coarse and fairly thick. The beating marks are very distinct.

Large, sub-rectangular, dark brown piece of barkcloth with black patterning on one side and patches of similar barkcloth stitched in. The central pattern consist of spots in concentric circles, organised into four vertical rectangles separated by double lines. The central pattern is bordered on the long edges by narrow rectangles that are divided into triangles and filled with dots and crescents. The design is wholly bordered by straight lines forming concentric rectangles, which are filled with dots and diagonal lines.

other.title: Mchila Wa Ngondo. Power object; a war-tail comprising an eland tail attached to a bundle wrapped with plaited plant fibre, plugged at one end with a cylinder of wood, with a group seven animal claws set into a dark material at the end. The bundle is described on the catalogue card as 'containing a piece of the heart of a nobleman, and many other medicines, mostly burnt, put into five small antelope horns.'

Powder horn with wooden stoppers at each end; two horn projections at widest end with two circular perforations in each. Centre of horn circumferentially grooved and wrapped with plant fibre cord which is looped through the wooden cap. Leather belt wrapped around horn and secured with a metal buckle.
Wooden board used to teach Arabic reading and writing. Rectangular with two short feet and a lonzenge-shaped handle.
Powder horn with wooden base. Two raised rings around narrower part. Point cut off and open. Four circular perforations just below rim.
